The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the
injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 31.07.2018.
2. The case of the Petitioner in brief

is that, on 31.07.2018 at about 06.00 a.m., one Mr.Mathew was going on morning walk on BegurKoppa road from his house situated at Diamond Archeries Feed Mill he noticed that the petitioner was riding the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA 13EF6814 was proceeding on BegurKoppa road, at that time a Car bearing Reg.No.KA51ML9612 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner coming from Koppa towards Begur on the same road hit the two wheeler head on.
Due to the said accident the rider of the bike fell on the left side of the road and sustained head injury and after the accident the Driver of the car did not stop the car and sped away.

Thereafter he was shifted to the hospital and Mr.Mathew observed the white number plate of the Car which was cut into two pieces having black letters written on it and handed over the said number plate to the police station and requested the police to identify the car and Driver with the help of number plate.

The Bannerghatta police registered a case in their Cr.No.0138/2018 against the Driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA51ML9612 punishable u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
3.

It is further case of the petitioner that, immediately he was shifted to Vijayashree Hospital and treated for severe head injury, right femur shaft fracture, right tibia shaft fracture, left clavicle fracture as an inpatient for 2 days from 31.07.2018 to 01.08.2018 and thereafter he was shifted to Manipal hospital for further treatment and was admitted as an inpatient from 01.08.2018 to 10.08.2018 i.e., for 10 days and diagnosed with polytrauma RTA, left Temporo parietal EDH, left Temporoparietal Calvarial fracture, Left Aygomatic Arch Fracture, left greater wing of sphenoid fracture, left Mid 1/3rd of shaft of clavicle fracture, right mid shaft femur fracture displaced, right mid shaft tibia fracture and admitted in ICU and after taking DAMA he was shifted to Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre where right clacaneal steinman pin and traction applied and thereafter referred to MMH and thereafter with the reference of the Neuro Surgeon and Orthopedician he was shifted to MICU of neuro monitoring and management and discharged with advice.

4. The petitioner further pleaded that due to grievous injury resulted in permanent disability and he is not able to walk properly, stand/sit comfortably and has not able to pursue his avocation and due to head injury he is suffering from loss of memory and he is still suffering from pain in his legs, body and severe headache and became bedridden.

So far he has spent Rs.10,00,000/ towards medical,
transportation and other expenses.
Prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy, working at Drums department and earning Rs.32,000/ including O.T.

are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
5. In response to the summons, the Respondents have appeared through their respective counsels and filed written statement.

6. The Respondent No.1 in the written statement have denied the case of the petitioner as false and admitted issuance of policy but their liability is subject to terms and conditions and submitted that there is noncompliance of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further submitted that there a delay in lodging complaint and the FIR is lodged belatedly in order to search and falsely implicate the vehicle in the accident.

According to the averments of the petition the alleged accident took place on account of head on collisions of the two vehicles viz., car bearing Reg.No:KA 51ML9612 and motorcycle bearing Reg.No:KAEF6814 and there is negligence on the part of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No:KAEF6814 alone in respect of the alleged accident and the petitioner failed to make the owner and insurer of the said bike as party.
Therefore prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

7. The Respondent No.2 in the written statement has denied the averments made in para No.1 to 14 as false and submitted that the petitioner had sustained simple injuries as the petitioner colluded with the duty doctors and with a malafide intention the injuries had been cooked up just to claim more compensation amount from the respondents by suppressing the real facts.

Further submitted that on 3.8.2018 the petitioner and the local villagers of the petitioner threatened her and extracted a sum of Rs.50,000/ from the respondent No.2 and she somehow managed to take the receipt as acknowledgement for the payment of said amount from the wife of the petitioner.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the scooter and further the injuries sustained by him are simple and further she had borne the entire medical expenses to the petitioner at Vijayashree Hospital, inspite of that the petitioner has filed the fictitious petition.
At the time of accident, the Insurance policy was in force and valid and the same was duly insured with the first respondent.
Therefore prayed for dismissal of the petition against her.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA51ML9612 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 12. Issue No.1: The Petitioner in order to prove that the accident was occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA51ML9612 has examined himself as PW.1 and produced 4 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.4.

He has specifically stated in his evidence that, the first information is lodged stating that on 31.07.2018 morning at about 6.00 am one Mr.Mathew while was going morning walk on Begur - Koppa road from his house at that time the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA 13EF6814 was proceeding on Begur Koppa road, at that time a Car bearing Reg.No.KA51ML9612 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner coming from Koppa towards Begur on the same road hit the two wheeler head on and caused the accident.

On the other side, the Respondents have denied the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and specifically contended that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
In the cross examination of the PW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disbelieve the alleged manner of accident.

13. In support of the defence the respondent No.1 has examined its State head Legal and TP claims as RW.1 who has deposed in support of their defence that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
In the cross examination of RW.1 it is brought out that the accident road is only 20 feet width, as per the first information it is mentioned that the driver of the car fled away from the spot.
14. In the crossexamination of PW.1 nothing contrary admission are brought out.
Admittedly the RW.1 is not an eyewitness and the respondent No.1 has not lead evidence of eyewitness or other witnesses in support of their defence.

The RW.1 deposed based on the IMV report but as per the police documents itself it is mentioned that head on collision took place and no sketch is there to ascertain as to in which side of the road the accident occurred.
Therefore merely head on collision does not make or points any negligence on the part of the petitioner unless there is specific evidence in that regard.
Therefore, the evidence of RW.1 is not much helpful to the respondent No.2.
The respondent No.1 also not stepped into the witness box to prove her defence.

Further, the Petitioner apart from his oral evidence has produced the documents such as FIR and Complaint in Cr.No.138/2018 of Bannerghataa Police Station, complaint, charge sheet mahazar and IMV report as per Exs.P.1 to P.4.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.4 and appreciating them which are public documents having presumptive value under law, in absence of contrary evidence this court is of the opinion that the driver of the offending vehicle driven it with rash or negligent manner and caused accident as alleged by the claimant.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:

The Petitioner has further averred that, on account of accident, he has not healed up completely and is still suffering from pain in his legs, body and severe headache and has demising memory power due to the severe head injury caused at the time of accident and he is bed ridden and is taking assistance and suffering from permanent disability and hence he is unable to do his earlier work/occupation.
The Petitioner in this regard has entered into witness box and deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability.
Apart from that, he has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.5.
As per Ex.P.5, the petitioner has sustained, Severe head injury, right femur shaft fracture, right tibia shaft fracture and left clavicle fracture which are grievous in nature.
The petitioner has got examined Dr.Ramesh B. as PW.4.
This court while considering the Issue No.1 has already come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the driver of Car.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation from the Respondents.

DISABILITY:-
17.

The PW.4 - Dr.Ramesh B.  Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore, has produced OPD card and Xray as per Exs.P.30 and P.31 and he has deposed that, on verification of Discharge Summary the patient by name Shivananda gave history pf RTA pm 31.07.2018 and he has sustained (i)  Mid shaft femur displaced fracture,
(ii)  Mid Shaft tibia Fracture, (iii) Left Middle 1/3 fracture of left Clavicle and (iv) head injury and he has underwent treatment of internal fixation of (R) Femur and  Tibia, left clavicle fracture treated conservatively.

The PW.4 further deposed that he has examined him recently on 31.03.2022 for disability assessment and he complained of difficulty to squat on the floor, climb upstairs, walk on slope, sit cross legged with (R) lower limb, cannot walk without support, difficulty to do routine activities and on examination he found restriction of joint movements of (R) hip, flexion extension 50 degree normal 0140 degree, abduction abduction 20 degree, normal 075 degree, rotation 30 degree normal 085 degree, (R) knee flexion - extension 30 degree, normal 0145 degree, difficult to squat on floor, climb upstairs, kneel, sit cross legged, walk on slope, stand on affected limb and the radiological examination shows fractures united with implants in situ and the petitioner suffers from permanent physical disability of 48% of (R) lower limb, which is 24% of whole body and he need one more surgery for removal of implants.

In the cross examination of PW.4 it is brought out that, he has not treated the petitioner, the fractures are united, the tibia fracture is between the knee joint and ankle joint 9middle), the ROM is in hip joint and knee joint, the femur fracture is between the hip joint and knee joint (middle), he has not described the cause of ROM, he has not described the cogent reason for it, he has not mentioned the calculation for the percentage of disability to Sri.Y.B.Shankar @ Shivananda vs Authorized Representative on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28350592/

sentences.text: Therefore, considering the nature of injury, treatment taken, evidence lead, age of the petitioner, the 24% of whole body disability deposed by the PW.4 appears to be on higher side.
The PW.4 only deposed about the physical disability and not deposed as to how it affects the work of the petitioner.
The discharge summary shows that at the time of discharge the condition of the petitioner was stable.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the period of treatment that he has undergone, his age, the functional disability is considered at 12% to the whole body.
Monthly income 18.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working at Balmer Lawrie - Van Leer Limited, in Drums Department and getting salary of Rs.31,989/ per month.

To substantiate the income, he has produced salary slips as per Ex.P.14, P.23 and also produced salary slips form July 2018 to January 2019 issued as per Ex.P.34 and also examined Mr.L.H.Siddeshwara - Deputy General Manager and HR as PW.2 and produced Exs.P.27 to P.29, true copy of appointment letter,
copy of letter dated 15.11.2019 and copy of attendance register extract from the date of accident till report along with salary slips.

PW.2 has deposed that the petitioner was working in their company for past 20 years as power press operator who was appointed on 1.1.2001 and as the petitioner met with accident was absent fro work from 31.7.2018 to 01.01.2019 and was on leave for six months and the petitioner is not able to perform his earlier work as a Turner as the operator of a power press machine is required to stand and walk constantly for hours for his work before the machine for his work accomplishment.

The PW.2 has further deposed that as the petitioner sustained multiple fracture to his lower limbs so he is not able to stand constantly and do his machinery work as he used to do earlier and the Management on considering his disability on humanitarian grounds had been a chair and one single machine to operate instead of three machines, due to disability of the petitioner the company is also incurring loss by engaging another skilled machine operator in the place of the petitioner.

The PW.2 has further deposed that the petitioner had lost his capacity to excel his work and obtain promotion in his job and he had also lost his chance of getting more increments and incentives, due to the disability to stand before the turning machine and the petitioner has to bear the difficulty of high cost of living out of his meagre income till his retirement from the service and his future in the company is very bleak.

sentences.text: 20. As per the evidence of Pws.2 and 5 the petitioner is still working in the same company and getting salary but as per their evidence the petitioner is given with another job of less salary and the petitioner is drawing less salary compared to his earlier salary and the petitioner is entitled for increments and the petitioner took six months leave for which he was not paid salary.
In the cross examination the PW.5 clearly stated that the petitioner is working in the same job i.e., operator work and working for eight hours but unable to work overtime.

The PW.2 contrary to the evidence of PW.5 had deposed that the petitioner lost his chance of getting increments and incentives and the petitioner is operating single machine instead of three machines as earlier.

No doubt the true copies of the salary slips of the petitioner is produced which are of the months from July 2018, January 2019 to March 2019 and also produced the true copy of attendance register extract to show that the petitioner remained absent for six months to his work.

As per the case of the petitioner and evidence of Pws.2 and 5 the petitioner is given with less work and is paid with less salary when compared with earlier work and salary but to substantiate this except producing the salary slips and attendance register extract no other documents/basic documents are produced like order of the Management or HR department for having passed orders allotting less work job/single machine operator job to the petitioner by reducing his salary and any kind of order of said modification by the company is not produced.

In absence of such basic documents the salary slips and the attendance register extract is not sufficient to prove the case of the petitioner that he is given with less work job and less salary compared to earlier.

Therefore, on appreciating the evidence as discussed above, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is continued in the same job and getting salary and also getting increments and there is no any loss of income to the petitioner.

Further the PW.1 stated that he has not produced the recent salary slips and from this an adverse inference can be drawn that as there is a hike in his salary and hence he has not produced the recent salary slips as it produced will go against his case.
Therefore, the petitioner has proved that he was getting salary of Rs.31,989/ as on the date of accident but failed to prove that he is getting less salary and there is no any hike in his salary.
As per the above discussion the petitioner continued in the same job and hence he is not entitled for loss of future income.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Vijayashree Hospital,
treated as an inpatient for 2 days from 31.07.2018 to 01.08.2018 and thereafter he was shifted to Manipal Hospital for further treatment and treated as an inpatient for 10 days from 01.08.2018 till 10.08.2018 and thereafter he was shifted to Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre, treated for 7 days from 10.08.2018 to 16.08.2018, underwent physiotherapy and got discharged with advice.
Considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment he has underwent, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/ under this head.

ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded and deposed that he has spent more than a sum of Rs.10,00,000/ towards medical, transportation and other expenses.

In this regard,
he has produced 37 medical bills as per Ex.P.15 for a sum of Rs.8,25,404.50/ and also produced medical bills as per Ex.P.21 only for a sum of Rs.87,779/.
In total Rs.9,13,183/.
In the cross examination of PW.1 stated that he got Rs.75,000/ from Medical Insurance benefit but the PW.5 stated that the petitioner did medical insurance approximately for Rs.2,00,000/.

Therefore, in absence of specific evidence about as to how much amount he got under medi claim insurance and as to how much he paid personally no compensation can be awarded to the petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled any compensation under the heads of Medical Expenses.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained severe head injury, right femur shaft fracture, right tibia shaft fracture and left clavicle fracture as per Ex.P.5.
As per the claim of the petitioner, he has remained absent to his duty for six months and in support of the same he has examined Pws.2 and 5.
But except producing the attendance register extract specific evidence is not lead by the petitioner to prove that he was not paid any salary for the said period and he lost leave of six months.
Therefore, it appears that the petitioner got salary for the said absent/leave period/medical leave period of six months.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
As per the discussion made above, the petitioner has continued in the same job and getting the salary and hence this Tribunal is of the view that there is no loss of future income to him.
Therefore, he is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND DISCOMFORT AND UNHAPPINESS ON ACCOUNT OF DISABILITY:
The Petitioner was aged about 42 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries.
The Petitioner has to suffer the disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to loose some amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered a sum of Rs.80,000/ is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals as an inpatient.
In this regard he has produced discharge summaries as per Exs.P.6, P.18 and P.20.
As per these documents he was treated from 31.07.2018 to 01.08.2018 and from 01.08.2018 to 10.08.2018 and from 10.08.2018 to 16.08.2018 for total 17 days and discharged with an advice.

However, during this period he must have spent Sri.Y.B.Shankar @ Shivananda vs Authorized Representative on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28350592/
8
considerable amount on his conveyance, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of the PW.4, he needs another surgery for the removal of the implant.
But there is no estimation bill produced by the Petitioner or PW.4.
Looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.

21. The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/
2. Medical expenses  3. Loss of income during laid up  period 4. Loss of future income  5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.80,000/ discomfort and unhappiness on account of disabilities 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges 7.
Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/ TOTAL Rs.2,00,000/ and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.

LIABILITY:
22. The Respondent No.1 have not proved its defence by leading evidence.

Therefore,
the Respondents are being insurer and the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy is existed as on the date of accident, hence the respondent No.1/insurer is to indemnify the respondent No.2/insured and to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.2,00,000/ with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER

The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation shall be released in favour of the Petitioner on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the
injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 31.07.2018.
Due to the said accident the rider of the bike fell on the left side of the road and sustained head injury and after the accident the Driver of the car did not stop the car and sped away.
The Bannerghatta police registered a case in their Cr.No.0138/2018 against the Driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA51ML9612 punishable u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
3.
6. The Respondent No.1 in the written statement have denied the case of the petitioner as false and admitted issuance of policy but their liability is subject to terms and conditions and submitted that there is noncompliance of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further submitted that there a delay in lodging complaint and the FIR is lodged belatedly in order to search and falsely implicate the vehicle in the accident.
Therefore prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.
7. The Respondent No.2 in the written statement has denied the averments made in para No.1 to 14 as false and submitted that the petitioner had sustained simple injuries as the petitioner colluded with the duty doctors and with a malafide intention the injuries had been cooked up just to claim more compensation amount from the respondents by suppressing the real facts.
Further submitted that on 3.8.2018 the petitioner and the local villagers of the petitioner threatened her and extracted a sum of Rs.50,000/ from the respondent No.2 and she somehow managed to take the receipt as acknowledgement for the payment of said amount from the wife of the petitioner.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the scooter and further the injuries sustained by him are simple and further she had borne the entire medical expenses to the petitioner at Vijayashree Hospital, inspite of that the petitioner has filed the fictitious petition.
At the time of accident, the Insurance policy was in force and valid and the same was duly insured with the first respondent.
opennyai_summary.issue:
8. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA51ML9612 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3.
What order or award?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
13. In support of the defence the respondent No.1 has examined its State head Legal and TP claims as RW.1 who has deposed in support of their defence that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner himself.
The Petitioner has pleaded and deposed that he has spent more than a sum of Rs.10,00,000/ towards medical, transportation and other expenses.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore merely head on collision does not make or points any negligence on the part of the petitioner unless there is specific evidence in that regard.
Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.4 and appreciating them which are public documents having presumptive value under law, in absence of contrary evidence this court is of the opinion that the driver of the offending vehicle driven it with rash or negligent manner and caused accident as alleged by the claimant.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation from the Respondents.
In absence of such basic documents the salary slips and the attendance register extract is not sufficient to prove the case of the petitioner that he is given with less work job and less salary compared to earlier.
Therefore, on appreciating the evidence as discussed above, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is continued in the same job and getting salary and also getting increments and there is no any loss of income to the petitioner.
Further the PW.1 stated that he has not produced the recent salary slips and from this an adverse inference can be drawn that as there is a hike in his salary and hence he has not produced the recent salary slips as it produced will go against his case.
Therefore, the petitioner has proved that he was getting salary of Rs.31,989/ as on the date of accident but failed to prove that he is getting less salary and there is no any hike in his salary.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:
Therefore, he is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
The Petitioner was aged about 42 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
21. The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/
2. Medical expenses  3. Loss of income during laid up  period 4. Loss of future income  5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.80,000/ discomfort and unhappiness on account of disabilities 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges 7.
Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/ TOTAL Rs.2,00,000/ and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.
Therefore,
the Respondents are being insurer and the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy is existed as on the date of accident, hence the respondent No.1/insurer is to indemnify the respondent No.2/insured and to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/ but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.2,00,000/ with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.2,00,000/ (Rupees Two Lakhs only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.1/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation shall be released in favour of the Petitioner on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
